column1: It's called a rare earth magnet.
Mostly iron, a pinch of boron, and a metal called neodymium.
It's small, but it's very strong.
And in a motor, strength is everything.
A stronger magnet gives you the same push from a smaller motor.
And lighter means you get more kilometres on one charge.
That's why most electric scooters and cars you see on the road use these magnets in their motors.
The same kind of magnet sits in your phone's little vibration motor, in many wind turbines, and in defence systems.
India needs about four thousand tonnes of these magnets a year... and we buy almost all of them from abroad.
And more than eight out of every ten come from one country.
So you're probably thinking — if the sand is ours, why can't we just dig it up and make them?
